reason: Every measured claim checks out against the source and the driven page. b.css declares background: var(--back) then overrides it with background: var(--fore-06) six lines later, directly contradicting the comment above it; computed background-color of .b-edit is rgba(255,255,255,0.06) at 390/768/1280/1440. Driving owner-editing, exactly three foreign .b-title runs intersect the panel rectangle at 1280 and 1440 (Final dress fitting, Choose the evening music, Final guest numbers) and four at 390 (plus Venue walk-through); at 390 the panel measures 154x537 and the title input clips ('Send the invitations', scrollWidth 174 vs clientWidth 118). The cause is corroborated by four other seats, so it is not this finding's contribution; judged on its distinct additions the finding still stands, but the fix as written is wrong in three checkable ways and must not be applied verbatim. (1) The shadow is NOT barred by the register. Rule 4 reserves shadows for objects that genuinely float and this one does float by declaration and by z-index over an absolutely-positioned measure, so it is the sanctioned case. What kills the proposed value is arithmetic, not doctrine: rgba(0,0,0,0.32) fails the palette lock, because audit.mjs matches box-shadow rgba() against the three hexes at +/-1 per channel and black (0,0,0) is 17 off Ink (17,17,17) -- so this fix breaks a gate the master currently passes; and the approach room's ground is ink (.b-field computes rgb(17,17,17)), where any near-black shadow is a 6/255 step and reads as nothing. A drop shadow cannot express elevation on this ground at all. (2) Deleting the tint outright is a downgrade, not a fix: it leaves the plate at exactly the page ground with only a 16% hairline, a weaker object than the author intended. Opacity and lift are separable and should be separated. (3) The bottom-sheet geometry is right and its reserve mechanism is a no-op: shell.css sets * { box-sizing: border-box } and render-b.js gives .b-measure an inline explicit height (toDay*px + ROW), so padding-bottom there is absorbed into the declared height, moves nothing (abspos items position from the padding-box top) and reserves zero pixels. The sheet would still cover the last row, the behind block and the foot. .b-field has auto height and is the real scroll content, so that is where the reserve belongs. Position: fixed itself is safe -- no ancestor of .b-item carries transform, filter, contain or backdrop-filter -- and the sheet serves the locked idea rather than fighting it, since an unobstructed measure is what makes 'editing is moving something nearer' legible on a phone.
sharpenedFix: In b.css .b-edit, do not delete the tint -- make it opaque by layering it: replace `background: var(--fore-06);` with `background: linear-gradient(var(--fore-06), var(--fore-06)), var(--back);` and delete the now-dead earlier `background: var(--back);`. That is one line, keeps the intended lift, computes background-color to an opaque var(--back), and stays palette-legal in both rooms (--fore-06 is white on ink, ink on paper). Drop the hard-coded `0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.32)`: on the ink ground it is invisible and it fails the palette gate. If lift is still wanted, declare it once in shell.css beside the fore/back ladder as a ground-aware token -- paper room `0 8px 24px rgba(17,17,17,0.16)`, ink room an outward ring `0 0 0 1px var(--fore-16)` rather than a shadow, since nothing in the palette is darker than the ink ground -- and reference the token, never a literal. Keep the below-700px bottom sheet (position: fixed; left: 12px; right: 12px; bottom: 12px; max-height: 70svh; overflow-y: auto), which also dissolves the 154px stacking and the input clipping by giving the panel the full 366px, but move the reserve: on open, set the sheet's measured height as padding-bottom on .b-field (auto height, the actual scroll content), not on .b-measure, whose inline explicit height plus border-box sizing swallows padding entirely. Scroll the edited row into view above the sheet with `block: 'center'` and honour prefers-reduced-motion on that scroll. For the gate, the seat's first assertion is correct and cheap -- computed background-color alpha of .b-edit is 1 -- and the second should be widened past titles: no .b-item outside the edited one may intersect the .b-edit rectangle at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440 (at 390 four whole items overlap today, not just their titles), plus one assertion that at 390 the sheet's bottom edge sits above the last reachable content after the reserve is applied.
